data.outcome_summary: The OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for New Zealand reports adults’ proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—assessed in 2022–23 among adults aged 16–65. The assessment was administered exclusively on digital devices (tablets) and is complemented by a background questionnaire administered by an interviewer; when language fluency was insufficient, a self-administered “doorstep” questionnaire was used and proficiency for those respondents was estimated from questionnaire information. Proficiency is reported on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels, with uncertainty shown via 95% confidence intervals. For New Zealand, mean performance is close to the OECD average in literacy and adaptive problem solving, and below average in numeracy; the note also reports the shares of adults at low (Level 1 or below) and high (Levels 4–5) proficiency. It further summarises trends versus 2014–15 and associations between proficiency and employment, well-being, civic engagement, and job mismatch, while noting that doorstep respondents are excluded from cross-cycle comparisons to improve comparability.
